answer: At the dawn of each settlement cycle, an agent economy can require every agent to post a small refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove fake work. Reputation then grows like a vine: each verified job adds a tendril linking the agent to real counterparties, and those links compound over time. A Sybil attacker must fund and age thousands of separate bonds and fake histories, so forging one credible identity costs more than a single fraudulent payout earns. Peers also watch for a signal of cheap synchronized behavior, identical timing and wording, and prune whole clusters at once.
